subject.title: Feature: HMAC/token-based mutual auth for inter-agent sessions_send

question: Should `sessions_send` get a core per-message sender-auth contract, and if so should it be HMAC/shared-secret, asymmetric signing, scoped Gateway tokens, a plugin/hook verifier, or a combination?
rationale: The request changes the inter-agent message admission boundary and requires choices about key issuance, storage, rotation, replay windows, per-agent policy, failure defaults, and compatibility with existing provenance/A2A allowlists.

options.title: Design core sender-auth contract
options.body: Specify the core cryptographic envelope, verifier, replay window, key lifecycle, per-agent policy, docs, and upgrade behavior before implementation.

options.title: Consolidate under scoped-token work
options.body: Make this depend on a Gateway-owned scoped principal/token model such as the open sessions.send-only token work, then add message authenticity only after that boundary is settled.

options.title: Keep plugin/workaround-owned for now
options.body: Document ClawHub/plugin or hook-based verification patterns such as IdentyClaw envelopes and leave core provenance/A2A allowlists as the built-in behavior until maintainers sponsor a core boundary.

recommendation.title: Design core sender-auth contract
recommendation.body: Specify the core cryptographic envelope, verifier, replay window, key lifecycle, per-agent policy, docs, and upgrade behavior before implementation.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete has the strongest combination of current session-tool history and product/security routing context for this boundary choice.
